newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila extends Mindanao ceasefire for a week.
newsitem.headline: Manila extends Mindanao ceasefire for a week.

text.p: The Philippines on Tuesday extended a ceasefire on parts of Mindanao island for one week but rejected Moslem rebel demands for soldiers to withdraw from a captured guerrilla camp as a condition for resuming peace talks.
"Let us sit down again together and discuss, instead of (making) pre-conditions," President Fidel Ramos told reporters during a visit to the remote southern island of Tawi-tawi.

In Manila, armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said the military was extending for a week starting on Tuesday its unilateral ceasefire in two provinces of Mindanao to allow rebels to treat their wounded and hasten the resumption of stalled talks.
The extension will also allow 30,000 villagers who fled during the recent fighting to return to their homes, he said.
"What is only left is for them (the rebels) to lay down their arms and go back to the negotiating table," Acedera said.

The Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) scrapped exploratory peace talks with Manila last month after the military captured a major rebel camp in Maguindanao. The meeting was to discuss proposals for a general ceasefire across Mindanao and to draw up an agenda for formal peace negotiations.
The military said more than 70 guerrillas and 15 soldiers died in two weeks of fighting in North Cotabato and Maguindanao provinces. The MILF said 20 of its members died.
The MILF, with an estimated 8,000 fighters, is a breakaway guerrilla faction fighting for an Islamic state.
It was a not party to the peace deal signed by Manila last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).
